reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: APC initiates, KRAS grows, TP53 completes the adenoma carcinoma sequence
Hundreds of polyps by teens mean FAP needing prophylactic colectomy
Lynch cancers are microsatellite unstable and right sided with family endometrial cancer
CEA monitors recurrence; it never screens for colorectal cancer
reference.pathophysiology: Wnt pathway activation from APC loss lets crypt cells proliferate into adenomas accumulating KRAS, SMAD and TP53 hits toward invasion through muscularis mucosae. Mismatch repair failure instead accelerates mutation across microsatellites, while serrated lesions methylate and silence repair genes through BRAF driven pathways.
additionalDifferentials: FAP versus Lynch polyp burden and inheritance clues
Right versus left sided cancer presentations
Adenoma versus hamartomatous versus serrated polyps
additionalInvestigations: Tumour mismatch repair immunohistochemistry and germline testing
